summary: How YouTube's recommendation algorithm, tuned from 2011 onward to maximise watch time, steered viewers toward far-right propaganda, conspiracy theories and sexualised videos of children while the company denied the problem and underfunded moderation.

evidence.note: algorithm changes said to begin in 2010
Leanback autoplay launched in 2011, then watch-time ranking in 2012
former Google engineer Chaslot's account of the recommendation team
Google Brain integration and the boost it gave Alex Jones and conspiracy content
Reinforce learning system and far-right red-pilling via game and film reviews
segment on Molyneux and his drift to white nationalism
chief product officer Mohan denies the rabbit-hole effect
2019 reports that recommendations funnelled viewers to videos of children
outsourced moderators, contractor terms and their working conditions

notes: Primary subject is a company, so roles are empty. Despite the title, the story covers the broad far right rather than German Nazism, so fascism-far-right is used instead of nazism. YouTube's 2005 founding and early years get only a passing mention. Microsoft's Tay is an opening comparison and is not counted in the span.
